title: Coyote fallback sequence — rapid reference for solo night coverage
content:
Purpose:
Quick, intentionally terse notes for the person covering late-night/Solo Coyote runs. Not a replacement for the full runbook (see Confluence link above) — this is a stripped-down decision tree and the exact commands I reach for when latency spikes, model errors, or infra flaps during quiet hours.

Context / mental model:
- We have a three-tier fallback: 1) keep-hosted (same model, different host pool), 2) model-variant fallback (smaller quantized variant), 3) HTTP proxy to upstream-hosted (Redwood-hosted public endpoint) for critical user flows.
- Goal: restore user-facing traffic within 5–10 minutes for P0/P1 and minimize token spend during fallback.
- When in doubt, favor availability over cost during the first 15 minutes; tighten after stabilization.

Quick triage checklist (0–10 min):
1) Determine scope: single instance? AZ? whole pool?  (grafana service-ops -> cluster-latency, model-error-rate)
2) Check recent deploys: /deployments page and last 15m CI events (if any).
3) Ramp traffic policy? (console -> rollouts) - has an automatic rollback kicked?
4) If 50%+ error rate on a route -> consider immediate model-variant fallback for that route only.

Common incidents and my condensed actions:
- High model latency (p50 fine, p95 skyrockets):
  * Check runtime metrics: grpc queue length, kernel timeouts, GPU mem spikes.
  * If gRPC queue > 250 for >2m, enable route-level batching cap: set MAX_BATCH_MS to 8ms for that route. Commands: 
    - kubectl -n inference exec -it $POD -- /bin/sh -c "export MAX_BATCH_MS=8 && curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/config/reload"
  * If queue persists, scale up Dedicated pool by +1 replica in same AZ. Use console-scaling or CLI: 
    - rictl scale ded-pool/<pool-id> --replicas +1 --reason "p95 latency spike"
- OOM / GPU OOM observed:
  * If single pod OOM, cordon pod and drain to avoid noisy neighbor restarts. Patch pod annotation to prevent immediate restart: kubectl annotate pod $POD ops/skip-restart=true
  * Switch affected routes to fallback model-variant (quantized). Steps: console -> route -> override model -> select <model>-q4_0. Quick CLI: ri api routes update --route <route-name> --model <model>-q4_0
- Model returning garbage or hallucinating more (sudden regressions):
  * Check recent model deployments and traffic split. If a recent rollout hit, revert to stable tag. Console rollback or: ri api models rollback --model <model> --to-tag stable-2025-01-02
  * Trigger a temporary eval-suite run against the route to collect failing prompts and open ENG ticket.
- Host unreachable / network flaps in region: 
  * Failover by region: toggle routing policy to fallback-region (console quick action). If console unavailable, use CLI: rictl routes set-routing --route <r> --policy region:fallback-eu
  * For total region outage, flip critical routes to public-hosted upstream: set upstream_url to https://api.redwood-hosted.com/v1/generate (route-level override). Note: must add cost-note in incident summary.

Minimal commands cheat sheet (copy-paste friendly):
- Check pod logs (p95 errors): kubectl -n inference logs --tail=200 $POD
- Check queue metric (quick): rictl metrics query --metric grpc_queue_len --range 15m --filter pod=$POD
- Set route model fallback (CLI): ri api routes update --route orders-completion --model starling-base-q4_0
- Scale dedicated pool: rictl scale ded-pool/pool-42 --replicas 4 --reason "night p95 spike"

Communication plan (what I actually type in Slack):
- Channel: #oncall-night (pinned incident template exists)
- First message (quick): "p95 latency on /v1/generate (orders) -> investigating. Applying route-level fallback to starling-base-q4_0. ETA 10m. @eng-sre"
- After mitigation: "Mitigation applied: route fallback -> q4_0. p95 reduced from 4.3s to 0.9s. Monitoring for 20m before rollback to mainline."
- If escalation: ping @oncall-rotation (if after 02:00 PT) or call pager duty if P0.

Temporary procedures to leave for next shift (what I write in post-incident notes):
- Timeline: list timestamps for key actions and first observed metric.
- Commands executed (exact CLI lines) + stdout where relevant.
- Links to logs (grafana, loki queries) and the incident ticket created.
- Cost note: estimate extra tokens / upstream cost while on hosted fallback.

Known loose ends (things to finish later):
- Add automated route-level rollback after health is restored (ticket ENG-4123). Right now we do it manually.
- Create smaller q4 quant profile for 2k token paths (current q4_0 still expensive for long tokens).
- Hook quick action in Slack to flip to public-hosted upstream for critical routes (low-friction button).

My personal heuristics / rules of thumb (why I pick actions above):
- Small persistent p95 increases -> tweak batching or add a replica. Big sudden jumps -> fallback model variant.
- If failure surface is narrow (single route) prefer route-scoped changes to avoid unnecessary churn.
- Keep the first 10 minutes focused on availability; tighten cost after 20m if stable.

Post-incident checklist (to run within 24h):
- Create incident ticket and link logs (if not auto-created).
- Add an eval test captured prompts showing regression, add to regression-buckets.
- Run retrospective (quick 15–30m) and add the short postmortem note to the ticket.
- If root cause is infra (not model), create follow-up with infra team and assign oncall for follow-through.

Notes to self (untidy):
- Remember: when flipping to hosted upstream, set short TTL on cached embeddings for affected routes (so downstream UX doesn't get stale).
- If you see steady errors with KV cache misses, check memcached eviction rates. CMD: rictl metrics query --metric memcache_evictions --range 60m
- If you wake someone: give them concise summary + actions done + current state. They don't need raw logs in the first message.

Unresolved questions (add to morning triage):
- Should we automate route fallback only for specific customers? (privacy/cost tradeoff)
- When do we prefer autoscaler vs manual scale during nights? thresholds need formalizing.

If you are me at 03:12am and scared:
- Breathe. restore minimal customer experience first. Document everything. Leave a clear handoff note for morning (time, actions, links).

End of page — paper trail for the morning: paste this into the ticket and the #oncall-night handoff message.
